In your app

There are three ways to show a document, from most to least interactive:

Where Use What the reader gets
A React app mkp-react.js The document, drawn live, in MKP's look or your components.
Any other page or framework mkp-dom.js The same, mounted into an element.
No app mkp build --target html, md or html-md One offline page, or plain Markdown.

Each starts from the release's web files in one folder, say vendor/mkp/ (Getting started).

#Compile

A document is compiled into a bundle, either in the app or ahead of time:

import { compile } from './vendor/mkp/mkp.js';

const c = compile({ packs: [] });
const bundle = c.document(source, 'lesson.mkp.md');
if (!bundle) console.error(c.diags.errors);

Ahead of time, mkp build lesson.mkp.md --target ir writes lesson.ir.json, the same bundle as a file. An app that only shows documents can import that and leave the compiler out.

#React

import { MkpDocument } from './vendor/mkp/mkp-react.js';

export function Lesson({ bundle }) {
  return <MkpDocument bundle={bundle} theme="auto" options={{ onSignal: (e) => console.log(e.name, e.payload) }} />;
}

MkpDocument writes its own styles; there is nothing to import. Give it tokens to set your colours, spaces and corners by name, components to draw the base set with your own design system, and theme (light, dark or auto). It works in Next.js and every other React framework.

#Any other framework, or none

mkp-dom.js draws the same document into an element. It brings its own React, so the page needs none:

import { mount } from './vendor/mkp/mkp-dom.js';

const view = mount(document.getElementById('lesson'), bundle, {
  theme: 'auto',
  tokens: { space: { m: { value: 12 } } },
  onSignal: (e) => console.log(e.name, e.payload),
});
view.update({ theme: 'dark' });   // the reader's place stays
view.setBundle(next);             // another document starts afresh
view.unmount();

view.ready resolves once the document is drawn. The maths engine loads first only when the document has maths its build has not already typeset. The recipes wrap this in a component for Vue, Svelte, Solid, Angular and Astro.

To show the text and widgets before any script runs, build the document's first paint too (mkp build lesson.mkp.md --target ir,fragment --out out), put lesson.fragment.html in the element on the server, and mount the same build's bundle with hydrate: true. mount() takes the HTML over in place: nothing is swapped and nothing moves.

#Signals: the document talks to the app

A widget can tell the host app what the reader did: an answer checked, a step reached. It declares a signal and sends it; the app hears it in onSignal:

onSignal: (e) => {
  // e.name: 'answered', e.payload: { correct: true, value: 'Oslo' }, e.block: which block sent it
  if (e.name === 'answered') saveProgress(e.payload);
}

Check an answer in the examples sends one; its Signals panel shows them as they arrive.

#No app: pages and Markdown

node mkp-cli.mjs build lesson.mkp.md --target html --out site      # site/lesson.html
node mkp-cli.mjs build lesson.mkp.md --target md --out site        # site/lesson.md
node mkp-cli.mjs build lesson.mkp.md --target html-md --out site   # site/lesson.md.html
  • html is one offline page that draws the document, follows the reader's light or dark setting, and holds its Markdown for readers with scripts off.
  • md is the Markdown a reader without MKP gets: every widget as its text. --no-answers leaves answers out.
  • html-md is that Markdown drawn as HTML, maths as pictures, with no script at all.

These docs are built the html-md way: written in MKP, compiled once, served as static pages.
